claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child. Her name is Alex and she's 3 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that actually - my living situation is a bit complicated at the moment and I'm not certain how to answer that question in terms of Child Benefit rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - living situations can indeed be complicated. Let me ask a different question that might help clarify things:

**Can you tell me where you are physically residing at the moment, and roughly how long you've been there (or plan to be there)?** 

For example, are you currently in the UK but perhaps traveling frequently, or are you living abroad, or perhaps moving between countries? Any details about your situation would help me understand better.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I can tell you that Alex lives with me, and she's only 3 so she needs me to look after her full-time. But as for where exactly we're living and whether that counts as being in the UK for these purposes - I'm genuinely not sure how to answer that. It's part of why I'm trying to find out about eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you sharing that, and I understand the uncertainty. Let me try to help clarify what information is needed.

For Child Benefit eligibility, one of the key requirements is that you "live in the UK." This generally means you are physically residing in the UK on a regular basis.

**Are you and Alex currently physically present in the UK (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland) most of the time?** 

If you're unsure whether your specific situation counts as "living in the UK" for benefit purposes (for example, if you're temporarily abroad, or have an unusual living arrangement), just let me know the basic facts - such as which country or countries you're currently in - and I can help determine if we have enough information to assess eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I really don't know how to answer that question. I understand you need to know, but I genuinely can't say for certain whether we're in the UK most of the time or not. That's honestly part of my confusion about all of this.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - thank you for being honest about your uncertainty. 

The issue is that whether you live in the UK is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility. Without being able to establish your residency situation, I cannot determine whether you would be eligible or not.

Let me ask one more question to see if there's any other information that might help:

**Is there any other aspect of your situation that you ARE certain about that might be relevant?** For example:
- Are you responsible for Alex's care and paying for her needs (food, clothing, etc.)?
- Is Alex under 16 years old? (I know you mentioned she's 3, so this would be yes)
- Are there any other circumstances affecting Alex - such as being in hospital, in care, or living with someone else?

If you truly cannot provide information about your residency status, I may need to conclude that there's insufficient information to make a determination about eligibility.
